title: Why Bonds Respond To The Fed, Not To Inflation
text:
Why Bonds Respond To The Fed, Not To Inflation

Anatole Kaletsky

Gavekal Research | 20 Oct 2026

Exactly two weeks ago, I argued that the worst bear market for bonds since the 1970s was due for at least a tactical reprieve because investors were overestimating the number of Federal Reserve rate hikes likely in the year or so ahead (see Reasons To Start Buying Bonds). By sheer good luck, the US bond market turned on that very day. The 10-year yield peaked on October 6 at 5.31%, and declined to 5.09% by last Friday in response to a series of Fed comments that proved less hawkish than expected, before rebounding slightly on Monday.Better still for the view that bond prices these days are driven almost exclusively by Fed expectations, the past fortnight’s bond market rebound has occurred in a clearly deteriorating inflation environment, as evidenced by the shockingly bad US CPI and PPI data released last Wednesday.
